summaryText:
In week three of the Planted series, guest speaker Pastor Leo Bigger, visiting from Switzerland, taught on being planted in the house of God through the life of Moses. He explained that the name Moses means "the pulled out one," and that Moses' story shows how God pulls people out, calls them back, and plants them in his purposes. Even after failure, Pastor Leo said, the grace of God bounces us back into the game and sin does not have the final word.

Pastor Leo walked through a cycle that begins with an encounter with God. The first phase is doubt, when God's call feels impossible. Moses raised many objections, and Pastor Leo shared how God called him to lead a church when he felt unqualified. His encouragement was that feeling it is impossible can be the very place where God's calling begins.

The second phase is obedience. Pastor Leo pointed to Exodus 4:20, where Moses took the staff of God in his hand, and taught that when we say yes to God, something shifts from the natural to the supernatural. He called obedience the love language of God. He also reminded us that God sometimes moves us out of the comfort zone and into the blessing zone, much as a shepherd moves sheep to fresh pasture.

The third phase is struggle. Moses stepped out in faith and then faced resistance, and in Exodus 5:22-23 he honestly brought his confusion to the Lord. Pastor Leo described a "valley of disappointment" that many believers walk through when they are planted in a church, family, or ministry. He spoke with care about a season of deep grief after his church lost a beloved worship leader, and how that season tested his faith. His counsel was not to give disappointment a seat at the table, but to bring it honestly to God, who prepares a table even in the presence of our enemies (Psalm 23).

He closed by describing the full circle: encounter, doubt, obedience, struggle, the desert, and finally the promised land. Life is often found in the "in between," and we are always in transition, yet God is leading and about to do something new. Pastor Leo led the church in a prayer of surrender, inviting people to pour out their disappointments to Jesus and receive healing, peace, and hope. The service ended with an invitation to give one's life to Christ, and a reminder to complete the connection card, scan the QR code, and return next week as Pastor Travis continues the series.
mainPoints: God calls us, and when his call feels impossible, that is often where his work in us begins.
Obedience is the love language of God: when we say yes, he moves us from the natural to the supernatural and from comfort into blessing.
Struggle and disappointment are real, but we must not let them take a seat at our table, because God leads us through the valley and into his promise.

versesMentioned.text: So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey and started back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.

Moses returned to the Lord and said, "Lord, why have you brought trouble on this people? Is this why you sent me? Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought trouble on this people, and you have not rescued your people at all."

The Lord will make you the head, not the tail. If you pay attention to the commands of the Lord your God that I give you this day and carefully follow them, you will always be at the top, never at the bottom.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
Nehemiah said, "Go and enjoy choice food and sweet drinks, and send some to those who have nothing prepared. This day is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the Lord is your strength."
Surely your goodness and love will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.

Monday.scripture: Exodus 3:11 (NIV): "But Moses said to God, 'Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?'"
Monday.focus: When God's call feels impossible, it can be the very place his work begins.
Monday.action: Write down one area of life or calling that feels too big for you. Next to it, write one sentence about how God has already prepared you for it.
Monday.prayer: Lord, I feel small in the face of what you have called me to. Thank you that you do not call the qualified, you qualify the called. Help me trust you with what feels impossible. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Exodus 4:20 (NIV): "So Moses took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey and started back to Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand."
Tuesday.focus: Obedience is the love language of God, and our yes counts.
Tuesday.action: Choose one step of obedience you have been delaying, such as a conversation, a commitment, or a act of service, and take it today.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, I say yes to you today. Give me courage to take the next step you have shown me, even when it is uncomfortable. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Psalm 62:8 (NIV): "Trust in him at all times, you people; pour out your hearts to him, for God is our refuge."
Wednesday.focus: Moses brought his honest questions to God, and we can too.
Wednesday.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes. Tell God honestly about any disappointment, confusion, or hurt you are carrying, and then sit quietly and listen.
Wednesday.prayer: Lord, you know every disappointment I carry. I pour out my heart to you because you are my refuge. Heal what is wounded in me and help me trust you. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Psalm 23:5 (NIV): "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows."
Thursday.focus: Do not give disappointment a seat at your table.
Thursday.action: Name one disappointment that keeps replaying in your mind. Write it on paper, pray over it, and then set the paper aside as a symbol of releasing it to God.
Thursday.prayer: Jesus, I release my disappointments to you. I refuse to let bitterness or discouragement sit at my table. Fill my cup with your peace and goodness. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Psalm 23:4 (NIV): "Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me."
Friday.focus: God is with us in the valley, and we are always in transition toward his promise.
Friday.action: Send an encouraging message or make a short call to someone who may be in a hard season, and let them know you are praying for them.
Friday.prayer: Good Shepherd, thank you that you walk with me through every valley. Use me to remind someone else that they are not alone. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Psalm 92:13 (NIV): "Planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God."
Saturday.focus: Being planted in the house of God helps us flourish and keep going.
Saturday.action: Prepare your heart for Sunday. Pray for your church family, and consider inviting one person to join you or filling out the connection card.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, thank you for planting me in your house. Help me to grow, to stay connected, and to welcome others. Prepare my heart to worship you tomorrow. Amen.

title: Why You Keep Resisting God’s Plan | This Is What Happens When You Surrender
